title: Field Signal Anchorboard and Action Grid — customer asks synthesis
content:
Purpose:
This is a synthesis note (working/artifact) from the field signal sprint (Mar 8–12) — condensed into an "anchorboard" (key stable problems) and an "action grid" (proposed probes, owners, rough effort). Goal is to give PMs and ENG a compact, prioritized set of customer asks and low-cost probes we can run in the next 4 sprints.

Context and how this doc is different:
- Not a broad VOC dump; curated list of recurring, anchorable asks that are both high-impact and actionable.
- Includes quick experiments (1–2 week probes) and fallbacks that do not require large infra changes.
- Emphasis on customer quotes, severity, and an operational owner for immediate follow-up.

Methodology (notes):
- Sources: 18 customer calls, 42 CS support threads, 3 onboarding sessions, and two partner workshops.
- Timebox: 4 analysts (CS+Product) condensed signals into clusters, then mapped to anchor problems that surfaced repeatedly across customers and verticals.
- Bias: prioritize production-safety and developer-onboarding friction over pure feature parity.

Anchorboard (stable problems we keep returning to):
1) Lateral-degradation on complex prompt chains
   - Symptom: customers report that after 4–6 long-turn conversations, responses drift or hallucinate more often.
   - Who: fintech and knowledge-worker customers running multi-step retrieval+chain logic.
   - Quote: "We lose the thread after a few back-and-forths; the model starts inventing steps that don't exist."
   - Severity: High (can lead to lost trust / rollbacks).

2) Unclear billing spikes tied to reruns/cancellations
   - Symptom: Teams see intermittent token spikes after small client-side retries, unclear attribution in the console.
   - Who: mid-market SaaS customers with bursty usage patterns.
   - Quote: "We saw a $2k spike and couldn't tell if a retry bot or a model rerun caused it."
   - Severity: High (billing disputes).

3) Embedded-embedding search relevance drift
   - Symptom: Embedding results degrade after index refreshes or when using quantized models; retrieval precision varies by model variant.
   - Who: search/knowledge-base customers and internal partner teams.
   - Quote: "After we upgraded to the cheaper quantized model, our top-5 results were off."
   - Severity: Medium-High (product quality).

4) Limited observability on KV/prefix cache hits
   - Symptom: Teams can't tell if cache is working or why latency is spiky for identical prompts.
   - Who: platform teams and large customers on Dedicated.
   - Quote: "We don't know when prefix caching saved us tokens — we just see variance."
   - Severity: Medium

5) Rollout fallback semantics are confusing
   - Symptom: Canary and automatic fallback behavior sometimes causes sudden model switches with subtle API differences.
   - Who: customers using rollout/A-B policies via Console.
   - Quote: "We thought the canary would be isolated but a traffic shift changed outputs for some calls."
   - Severity: Medium

Action Grid (probes and recommended follow-ups — first 6 items are prioritized):
A. Quick telemetry patch: token-attribution pie (2 weeks, low effort)
   - Summary: Add a breakdown in Console that attributes token usage per request attempt and labels retries vs original attempts.
   - Owner: Hannah Lee (CS+Product)
   - Effort: Low (UI change + backend tagging)
   - Why: Directly addresses billing spike disputes and reduces CS escalations.
   - Risk: False positives if clients aggregate retries; include guidance text.

B. Conversation drift smoke-test harness (3 weeks, medium)
   - Summary: Automated test pipeline that replays multi-turn chains from customer-supplied transcripts to detect drift after N turns across model variants.
   - Owner: Marco Ruiz (Applied ML)
   - Effort: Medium (test infra + sample corpus)
   - Why: Reproducible regression detection and model selection guidance for customers.

C. Embedding-variant benchmark runner (2 weeks, low)
   - Summary: Small script and dashboard that shows recall delta when swapping quantized vs full models on customer's sample dataset.
   - Owner: Evan Brooks (Solutions Eng)
   - Effort: Low
   - Why: Gives an immediate, customer-facing data point to recommend quantization tradeoffs.

D. Cache-hit visibility beta (4 weeks, medium)
   - Summary: Add cache hit/miss counts and prefix-id in trace logs + Console surface for Dedicated.
   - Owner: Sana Gupta (Platform Eng)
   - Effort: Medium
   - Why: Reduces debugging time and ties into cost-reduction recommendations.

E. Rollout safety mode doc + UI affordance (2 weeks, low)
   - Summary: Short doc + toggle in Console for "strict canary isolation" that forces traffic partitioning.
   - Owner: Product-hosted-api (PM: TBD)
   - Effort: Low
   - Why: Quick mitigation to prevent surprise behavior during rollouts.

F. Customer trial: token budget sandbox (4 weeks, medium)
   - Summary: Per-route disposable token budgets for testing so customers can experiment without billing surprises.
   - Owner: Billing Infra (SRE)
   - Effort: Medium
   - Why: Helps adoption for early-stage teams and trialing new prompts.

Measurements and acceptance criteria (how we verify probes):
- Token-attribution pie: reduced billing disputes routed to CS by 60% in 30 days.
- Drift harness: detect >= 3 drift signatures across 10 sample transcripts; surface as daily alerts to Applied ML.
- Embedding runner: customers see a recall delta and mark recommended configuration in Console.
- Cache visibility: mean debug time for cache-related tickets drops by 40%.
- Rollout safety: zero surprise switches reported in first month for canaryed deployments.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are some of the drift issues caused by model prompt engineering at the customer layer rather than model serving? Need small customer interviews to disambiguate.
- Billing-attribution must consider third-party proxies and SDK retry logic — do we need server-side idempotency tags?
- How many customers will actually opt into a "strict isolation" toggle during rollouts? Risk of adoption friction.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Hannah to draft the Console microcopy and wireframe for token attribution (due 3/19).
- Marco to surface 10 candidate transcripts and sketch the replay harness (due 3/19).
- Evan to run embedding runner on 3 pilot customers and capture recall deltas (due 3/22).
- Sana to scope logs change and estimated SRE cost (due 3/24).
- Schedule 30-min sync with Product-hosted-api PM to align on rollout safety toggle (owner: Aisha).

Customer quotes folder (raw snippets):
- "We had to pause a release because the canary swapped in a model variant that changed outputs." (Large productivity app)
- "Our search quality dropped overnight when we flipped to cheap model — we need a way to test this on our data." (Enterprise search)
- "If you give us a clear breakdown we can resolve billing in minutes — right now it's a 2-day back-and-forth." (SaaS analytics)

Notes to self / TODOs for follow-up doc:
- Build a simple visualization mock of the token pie for the Console team review.
- Draft short customer-facing FAQ for rollout isolation to reduce support load.
- Consider adding a lightweight SDK flag for client-side idempotency tagging to make attribution more reliable.

Slack anchors / refs: #cs-field-signals, #product-hosted-api, #applied-ml-testbed

If this doc looks good, I'll convert to a Confluence page and open JIRA tickets for probes A–F next week.

End of note.
